citations.narrative:
A routine inspection was conducted at a USDA licensed facility that leases animals once a year for a pumpkin patch. A
traceback of the leased animals led to the discovery that the facility that leased the camel to the pumpkin patch for camel
rides, did not have a USDA license. The leasing facility that provided the camel had been licensed with other family
members in the past until 2008. This same facility got the camel from a current USDA licensed person. The facility
advised that they would like to apply for a USDA license in the future.
Continuing to conduct regulated activity without a license is a serious violation of the Animal Welfare Act. The lack of a
USDA license prevents the traceability and inspection of regulated animals to protect their health and well-being
according to the AWA regulations and standards.
No regulated activities may be conducted until a USDA license is obtained.
No person shall operate as a dealer, exhibitor, or operator of an auction sale, without a valid license.
To be corrected from this day October 1, 2026, forward
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with facility representative.
You may appeal all or part of any inspection report by submitting a written statement contesting the findings—along with
any supporting documentation—to the Deputy Administrator. Appeals of routine, focused, or attempted inspections must
be received within 21 days of report issuance as shown by the signature line of this report.
Appeals may be sent by email to AnimalCare@usda.gov.
Appeals sent by mail should be addressed to:
Deputy Administrator
APHIS Animal Care (AC)
U.S. Department of Agriculture
2150 Centre Avenue, Building B
Mailstop #3W11
Fort Collins, CO 80526-8117
